The model card calls REAX a decentralised lab on Bittensor subnet 92. It ran on our hardware through the maker's engine (the reax13 mode of reaxlabs/reax-engine at ff8f595, its own server, serve.py), both parts in FP8 (block-128) on one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, text only, one request at a time. rows.name: SubQ Snap 1.1
rows.latBasis: Median per request · 1 in flight · run · runs 346 · 1 questions/request
rows.method: Five option Turkish exam questions, scored against the published answer key. · SubQ Decisions API (public preview)
rows.limit: Questions come from one Turkish exam preparation book. Ranks follow the published table. Cost and calibration for a full run apply only to that run.
rows.tent: SubQ's subq-snap-1.1, in public preview, through its Decisions API, which also takes images. Its option probabilities arrive as 32-bit floats, so they sum to 1 only within 32-bit rounding. Its probability check used an experimental 32-bit rule of ours. For this model only, the check before its runs accepted a sum within one 32-bit epsilon (2^-23) per option when every value is an exact 32-bit float, instead of 7 decimal places; this is our tolerance, not an error bound SubQ states. The values are stored as SubQ returned them. It was paused twice while the approval of its probability check was confirmed, for 12 minutes and then for 3 hours 24 minutes, and resumed from its stored answers. The two requests in flight count those pauses in their times (706 and 12,236 seconds; the first after one retry, when SubQ had closed the connection), so the run's total request time and questions per minute include them. Without them, its median request time stays 0.378 s and its 90th percentile moves from 0.388 s to 0.387 s.

rows.name: Elephant-1
rows.latBasis: Median per request · 1 in flight · run · runs 373 · 1 questions/request
rows.costBasis: maker · at the maker's list price
rows.method: Five option Turkish exam questions, scored against the published answer key. · Base Labs server (qev, the model card's loader), self-hosted, BF16 · 1 × RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (96 GB); BF16
rows.limit: Questions come from one Turkish exam preparation book. Ranks follow the published table. Cost and calibration for a full run apply only to that run.
rows.tent: Base Labs' released elephant-1 weights (baselabs/elephant-1 at b3f8a93), a decision model post-trained from Qwen3.5-9B that also reads images. It ran on our hardware through its model card's loader (qev's DecisionEngine from OneJev at 81ce62f with the checkpoint's serve.patch, as the card's setup.sh installs it) behind our HTTP server (servers/baselabs_server.py), one request at a time. That runtime reads images only through an engine the patch leaves without the attention the model was trained with, so it is not on the Page images tab. The card mentions a trained "I don't know" option, but its answers have no such output, and our questions offer five options. Probabilities rounded to 6 decimals by the model's own loader. They sum to 1 only within that rounding, and the check before its runs allowed for it. Its card lists English only.

rows.tent: Liquid AI's released d1-2B weights (LiquidAI/d1-2B at 10e7671), a decision model built on LFM3-VL-2B that also reads images. It ran on our hardware through its model card's own call (model.system_one, Liquid's model code in Transformers) behind our HTTP server (servers/d1_server.py), one request at a time. Liquid lists 16 languages for it; Turkish is not among them. Its request times come from one GPU with no other known work while its runs took place, though the GPU was not monitored throughout. Only this model's server showed on it at 11:55 UTC on 1 November 2026, before the runs, and nothing at 12:35 UTC, after them; the one other project with a claim on that GPU confirmed it ran nothing there in between.

rows.method: Five option Turkish exam questions, scored against the published answer key. · GLiClass server (our servers/gliclass_server.py: the card's gliclass pipeline and its System One mapping), self-hosted, BF16 · 1 × DGX Spark, GB10 (128 GB unified memory); BF16
rows.limit: Questions come from one Turkish exam preparation book. Ranks follow the published table. Cost and calibration for a full run apply only to that run.
rows.tent: Knowledgator's released GLiClass v4 Edge (knowledgator/gliclass-v4-edge at 885af1a), a zero-shot classifier fine-tuned from DeBERTa-v3-large (supervised training, reinforcement learning, then a calibrator). Its card serves it as a library pipeline (gliclass) and maps a decision request onto it: the passage is the text, the instructions the prompt, each option a label, and a softmax over the calibrated label scores. It ran on our hardware (one DGX Spark), one request at a time, through our HTTP server (servers/gliclass_server.py) with that mapping and gliclass 0.1.22, in BF16, text only; a request over 16,384 tokens (the card's limit) is refused, never cut. Its card lists English only.
